headline: Romania shoots down a drone for the first time

sources.title: Romanian F-16 shoots down drone after airspace breach, marking first for NATO ally
F-16 downs drone in Romania's airspace for first time
Romania says F-16 shot down drone over the country's airspace (video, euronews)

chunks.text: A Romanian air force F-16 {{shot down}} a drone over Buzau County on Friday, July 24. Radar {{picked up}} the [[aircraft]] at 9:39 a.m., about 20 kilometers east of Sulina, and the pilot destroyed it with a [[missile]] at 11:02 a.m. The drone {{came down}} near the village of Padina. Foreign Minister Oana Toiu said it was the first time a drone had been [[intercepted]] and destroyed inside Romania's national [[airspace]].

verbs.correct: To destroy an aircraft by firing at it
verbs.wrong: To fire a warning shot into the air
verbs.why: Fighter jets shoot down planes, missiles, and drones that threaten a country's airspace. Over Romania, an F-16 shot down a drone that had crossed the border from the east.

verbs.correct: To detect a signal or object
verbs.wrong: To choose one thing from a group
verbs.why: Radios pick up weak signals, and radar picks up small objects far away in the sky. Romanian radar picked up the drone at 9:39 a.m., about 20 kilometers east of Sulina.

verbs.correct: To fall from the sky and land
verbs.why: Rain comes down in a storm, a kite comes down after the wind dies, and a damaged plane comes down fast. The drone came down near the village of Padina in eastern Romania.

chunks.text: Romania [[borders]] Ukraine and sits on the eastern edge of NATO, the military [[alliance]] whose members agree to defend one another. Romania takes part in a NATO air policing mission, in which allied jets help [[guard]] each other's skies. During the incident, Italian Eurofighter Typhoons were in the air, and two more Romanian F-16s tracked the drone. Reports of drones crossing into Romanian airspace, or of [[debris]] landing on Romanian [[soil]], {{go back to}} 2022, and officials have counted [[dozens of]] them.

verbs.correct: To date from an earlier time
verbs.wrong: To happen only one time before
verbs.why: A family recipe goes back to a grandmother, and an old friendship goes back to childhood. Reports of drones entering Romanian airspace go back to 2022, years before this recent incident.

chunks.text: Romania's army chief said the drone [[appeared to be]] a Shahed-type aircraft, an Iranian design that Russia has used [[in large numbers]] in Ukraine. That is a description of the shape, not [[proof]] of who sent it. Interim Defense Minister Radu Miruta said officials had not been able to {{pin down}} the drone's [[origin]]. He [[praised]] the crews for their "professionalism, [[composure]] and [[rapid]] response." President Nicusor Dan said the area was [[uninhabited]].

verbs.wrong: To write information down on paper
verbs.why: Investigators try to pin down a cause, a date, or an exact location. Officials in Romania could not pin down where the drone had been launched from.

chunks.text: Investigators are {{combing through}} the [[wreckage]], and officials are still trying to {{find out}} where the drone was launched. Miruta {{called for}} more [[spending]] on air defense and on equipment [[designed to]] stop drones. For the villages under that airspace, Friday ended with the most basic question [[unanswered]]: no one in the government has said whose drone it was.

verbs.wrong: To guard the wreckage from onlookers
verbs.why: Investigators comb through old records, emails, and crime scenes looking for clues. In Romania, investigators combed through the drone's wreckage for any sign of its origin.
People find out the truth, a secret, or the reason behind bad news. Romanian officials are still trying to find out exactly who sent the drone.
Workers call for higher pay, and citizens often call for change after a scandal. After the incident, officials called for more spending on Romania's air defense.

mainIdea.s: A Romanian jet shot down a drone that entered the country's airspace, the first case there. Investigators are still trying to find out who sent it and where it was launched from.
mainIdea.why: The army destroyed the drone near Buzau County, and officials say this had never happened in Romania before. Miruta admitted that the drone's origin could not be pinned down.

mainIdea.s: A drone was shot down over Buzau County after officials said they had traced its launch to Russia. The aircraft came down near an empty village, and nobody on the ground was hurt.
mainIdea.why: Close, but no origin was confirmed. Officials could not pin down where the drone came from, and its shape only resembled a design Russia has used in Ukraine.

mainIdea.s: Poland shot down several drones that crossed its border last year, prompting NATO talks on eastern air defense. That event led allied jets to increase patrols near a neighboring war zone.
mainIdea.why: This is about an earlier Polish shootdown, not the Romanian one from July 2026. Romania's case was its first ever and happened on its own.

lines.text: Romania {{shot down}} a drone last week. First time ever inside its own airspace.
[[That's the strange part]]. Nobody knows yet. Radar {{picked up}} the aircraft near the coast, and an F-16 destroyed it with a missile about an hour later.
It {{came down}} near a village, in an uninhabited area. Nobody was hurt.
Reports of drones crossing into Romanian airspace {{go back to}} 2022, dozens of cases. But this is the first interception.
Do they know what kind of drone?
The army chief said it looked like a Shahed type, the design Russia uses in Ukraine. But that describes the shape, it isn't proof. Officials couldn't {{pin down}} the drone's origin.
Investigators are {{combing through}} the wreckage to {{find out}} where it was launched. And the defense minister {{called for}} more spending on air defense.
A NATO country shooting at an unknown drone. [[That's a little too close for comfort]].
